html:
On 7 June 1692 an earthquake struck Jamaica and much of Port Royal, the island's main town, slid into the sea. About 2,000 people died in the quake and a tsunami, and thousands more of disease in the weeks after.

Port Royal, built on a sand spit at the mouth of Kingston Harbour, had been the richest English town in the Americas, a home of buccaneers, merchants and the slave trade. Preachers called the disaster God's judgment on the wickedest city on earth.

Survivors moved across the harbour and founded Kingston, which became the commercial centre and later the capital. The sunken part of Port Royal is one of the best preserved underwater sites of the 17th century, studied by divers since the 1950s.
